items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: when you had your jazz band, when you had Kid Alpert's band... I played when they didn't have no drums. Mm-hmm. Didn't have no drums when I played with Johnny Gould in there.

ctx.x: Yeah. That's all the flag raised in the army. I saw a lot of flag raised in the Navy and something like that, but none of them, no flag raised.
Well, when you had your jazz band, when you had Kid Alpert's band, how many men in it would take down at once? Well, you know, so you played at once?

Yeah, yeah, at once, well, we always would get on and then you never take down at the blowing instrument. We'd take down. Mm-hmm. Take down one or two bars. Mm-hmm. And they didn't have much singing then. Yeah. Didn't have much singing then. You know, they had a pen of singing then. We'd take down and rest, pick up again. Then the trombone, take down, the clanner, take down and rest a while, you know. Mm-hmm. We got a hard job, something like that, you understand. We'd take down and rest, but no much singing, no…
